content.what_it_is: Fortran collection of ten masked Cartesian finite-difference kernels: first y/x derivatives with wide stencils (lines 63-79 and 90-106), centered first y/x derivatives (lines 116-158), centered yy/xy/xx second derivatives (lines 167-236), and wide-stencil mixed-xy, xx, and yy operators (lines 246-323). Every routine loops over caller-supplied inclusive bounds and multiplies its result by integer MASK; the wide operators access offsets through two cells.

verbatim_spans.text: !    DERIVATIVE_Y_High is subroutine to calculation first-derivative y with higher-order
!    DERIVATIVE_XY_HIGH is subroutine to calculation 4th-derivative xy
!    DERIVATIVE_XX_HIGH is subroutine to calculation 4th-derivative xx
!    DERIVATIVE_YY_HIGH is subroutine to calculation 4th-derivative yy

unresolved: The HIGH routine comments call DERIVATIVE_XY_HIGH, DERIVATIVE_XX_HIGH, and DERIVATIVE_YY_HIGH '4th-derivative' operators at lines 240, 274, and 301, but their formulas at lines 257-266, 292-293, and 318-319 compute a mixed second derivative or pure second derivatives using fourth-order-accurate stencils; derivative order and accuracy order are conflated.

DERIVATIVE_Y_High and DERIVATIVE_X_High are described as higher-order at lines 57 and 83, but coefficients [1,2,-2,-1]/(8h) in lines 74-75 and 101-102 have a nonzero cubic Taylor moment and therefore remain second-order accurate; the intended provenance of this nonstandard wide stencil is not stated.
Comments 'I assume no 2nd derivative' at lines 228 and 289 directly precede active xx second-derivative calculations at lines 231-232 and 292-293, so the comments contradict executable code.

All HIGH kernels access I or J offsets of plus/minus two at lines 74-75, 101-102, 257-266, 292-293, and 318-319, but their loops use the caller bounds without boundary checks; whether every caller supplies a two-cell halo is unresolved in this file.

DERIVATIVE_XY and DERIVATIVE_XY_HIGH assign tmp1 through tmp4 at lines 203-204 and 257-263 without local declarations under IMPLICIT NONE, so they must be module entities imported wholesale from PARAM. If PARAM storage is shared, concurrent calls are not reentrant/thread-safe; PARAM declarations are outside this file.

MASK is INTEGER at each declaration but is used as a multiplicative scale rather than a logical branch throughout; admissible values are not constrained here, so values other than 0 or 1 would rescale derivatives.
